title: Replacement of the Chemical Oxygen Generators by a Longer Duration Unit in the Passenger Service Units

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Substitution of the twelve minute chemical oxygen generator by a twenty-two minute unit across the passenger service units, opening up the extended overwater and high terrain routes several operators had been unable to fly.

sections.reason: Three operators moved this type onto routes that cross high terrain where the depressurisation escape profile takes longer than the twelve minute generator supports, and each of them had to accept an operational restriction to keep the route. A fourth operator asked for the same capability for an over-water sector. The generator itself had also become the second most common cabin item found expired at a scheduled inspection, because the twelve minute unit was fitted with a shorter shelf life than the rest of the passenger service unit contents, and the mismatch produced an out-of-phase replacement task nobody liked.
sections.description: The twelve minute generator is replaced by a twenty-two minute unit and the mask hose set is changed to match the higher flow at the start of the sequence. The generator D3520111793165 is superseded by the longer unit, the hose kit D3520115531984 replaces the delivered hoses and the outboard hose D3520117654228 is changed at every second row where the run is longest. The actuator D3520120132145 in the passenger service unit is replaced because the firing pin travel changes. Loop clamps LN551613K3 secure the longer hose run above the ceiling panel. Functional items 5070HE4 and 76HE1 are affected. Work is above the cabin ceiling in zones 231 and 263, with the passenger service unit panels dropped along the whole cabin length. Installation detail is on drawing D35201171837.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 18.4 kg for a typical three class layout, distributed along the cabin, with a longitudinal centre of gravity effect below the reporting threshold. No electrical load change. The generator is not interchangeable with the twelve minute unit because the firing mechanism and the mounting length both change, and a mixed installation within one passenger service unit is prohibited. The scheduled generator replacement task moves into phase with the rest of the passenger service unit contents, which removes one out-of-phase visit per aircraft per year. The flight crew limitation on maximum diversion time is revised.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN C00612 at the end of August 2023. Retrofit is by Service Bulletin CRN-35-2002 and needs the cabin out of service for two shifts because every passenger service unit is opened. Removed generators must be discharged and disposed of under the operator's own hazardous material procedure and are not returned.

type_data.balance_impact: Distributed along the cabin, longitudinal CG shift under 0.02 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN C00612, generator supply constrained the ramp for two months
